searchDocs.content: </> Graph.FromInstances( container: Instance ,-- A folder of nodes. options: GraphBuildOptions? ) → Pathfinder

interface GraphBuildOptions { LinkRadius: number?-- Studs within which two nodes are linked automatically when the link test passes. Default 24. AutoLink: boolean?-- Turn the automatic linking off to use only explicit links. Default true. Ignore: {Instance }?-- Instances the linking rays pass through (the node parts themselves always are). CanLink: (( a: Vector3 , b: Vector3 ) → boolean)?-- Replaces the ray test: return true when an agent can walk from a to b. Ask your navmesh here for anything but flat floors. Graph: GraphOptions?-- Options for the graph itself (NearestLimit, LineOfSight). }  Reads a graph out of the place. Every BasePart or Attachment directly under container is a node at its position (a part's position is lowered to its bottom face, rotation taken into account). An ObjectValue named Link under a node whose value is another node is a one-way link; add the reverse for two-way; a value outside the container is warned about and skipped. A Link with an Action or Label attribute, or an ObjectValue child named Instance, becomes a [Graph.GraphLink]: set Label = "Door" and point Instance at the door, and the step at that node carries both. With AutoLink, nodes within LinkRadius of each other are linked both ways when CanLink says so, or, without it, when a ray 1.5 studs up between them is clear. The ray test is a line-of-sight test, not a walkability test: it links across a pit and refuses a staircase, so on anything but flat floors give CanLink a real answer.

searchDocs.title: Simplify​
searchDocs.content: </> Navmesh.Simplify(path: Path) → Path-- A new path; the input is not modified. Removes interior Walk steps that lie on the straight line between the last kept step and the next one, so a mover walks one long segment instead of many short collinear ones. Pure. Always kept: the first and last step, every Jump or Custom step, every step with a Label, and the step immediately before a Jump (the jump origin matters). A path of two or fewer steps comes back as a copy.

searchDocs.title: CollapseLabels​
searchDocs.content: </> Navmesh.CollapseLabels(path: Path) → Path-- A new path; the input is not modified. Merges each run of consecutive steps that share a Label into the first of them, keeping its position. A PathfindingModifier labels every waypoint inside its volume, and waypoints sit a couple of studs apart, so a doorway would otherwise be two or three "Door" steps and a handler would run at each. A run is broken by an unlabelled step or a different label. Pure.

interface SeenByOptions { FieldOfView: number?-- The full angle of each observer's view cone. Default 100. Range: number?-- Studs. Default math.huge. Eye: ((root: BasePart ) → CFrame? )?-- Where an observer looks from. Default: the character's head, else its root (Perception.EyeOf). A game that replicates the camera returns it here. Ignore: {Instance }?-- What the sight ray passes through. Default nothing. Observers: {BasePart }?-- Who may be looking. Default Perception.AllAliveRoots, hidden players included. }  "Would anyone see it happen here?" The check to run before a stalker teleports, spawns or vanishes, so it only ever does so off screen. The Watched sense is the same question asked about the agent every tick; this is the one-off version about any point.

The angle is the true angle in three dimensions, so something high above is outside just as something off to the side is. A position at the origin counts as inside. interface InvestigateOptions { Target: string | Vector3 | (agent: Agent) → Vector3? -- Where to go: a blackboard or Data key such as "HeardPosition", a position, or a function. Read once on entry. Linger: number | {number}?-- Seconds to stand at the spot before Then. Default 0. Acknowledge: string?-- A blackboard key to Agent:Acknowledge on entry, such as "HeardAt", so the noise that brought the agent here does not count as new again. Speed: number?-- Set on entry. interface RoamOptions { Interest: Interest-- The map of points to roam. Required. Range: number?-- Studs beyond which a point scores nothing for distance. Default 120. Tags: {string}?-- Only points with one of these tags. Linger: number | {number}?-- Seconds to stand at each point before moving on. Default 1. searchDocs.title: Call MoveTo every tick​
searchDocs.content: A chase state should call agent:MoveTo(agent.Blackboard.SeenPosition) in Update, every tick. The Navigator decides when that turns into a plan; you do not. Calling it once in Enter works for a fixed point, and the navigator still retries if the mover gets stuck, but a moving target needs the fresh position.

searchDocs.title: Transitions before Update​
searchDocs.content: Transitions are checked first, in order, and the first true one wins. Update only runs when none fired. Put the important interrupts (attack range, lost the target) at the top of the list.

searchDocs.title: Memory lives in the blackboard​
searchDocs.content: Sight keeps SeenPosition for Memory seconds after losing the target, then clears it. A chase state that transitions out on SeenPosition == nil gets "run to where I last saw them, then give up" for free. Tune Memory per enemy; it is the difference between a stalker and a bloodhound.

searchDocs.title: Distance is not sight​
searchDocs.content: Proximity writes NearestDistance through walls; Sight writes SeenDistance only with a clear line. Use the first to decide an attack that does not care about walls (a scream, a shockwave) and the second for one that does.

searchDocs.title: Utility for targets, transitions for modes​
searchDocs.content: When a state must choose one of several things, score them with Utility.Bestand give the current choice a bonus consideration so the choice is sticky. Do not score the decision to attack or flee; write it as a transition, where you can read it.

searchDocs.title: Watch the tick​
searchDocs.content: The default tick is 0.1 seconds. A fast enemy that must freeze the instant it is seen (the Weeping Angel) runs at 0.05. A slow patroller is fine at 0.25. Senses cost raycasts per tick, so the tick is your budget knob.

searchDocs.title: Give the navmesh a second​
searchDocs.content: PathfindingService rebuilds its mesh lazily after parts are added. An agent spawned in the same frame as its map will fail its first plan; the navigator retries on its cadence, so this is harmless, but the playground waits a second before spawning so the first path is clean.

searchDocs.title: Straight legs walk off ledges only if you let them​
searchDocs.content: Straight checks for floor every few studs and projects its endpoints onto it. With FloorCheck off it is just a sweep, which is fine on a flat arena and wrong on a rooftop.

searchDocs.title: A kill is the finishing blow​
searchDocs.content: Attack.State with Kill = "Live" still does plain damage on every hit that does not finish the victim; the live kill only plays for the blow that would bring their health to zero. If you want every hit to be a kill, make Damage at least the victim's health.

searchDocs.title: return nil under strict​
searchDocs.content: Under --!strict with the brain annotated as VluxyAI.Brain, an Update must end withreturn nil when it stays put: the checker wants every path to return a string?. A state with only transitions needs no Update at all, which is the shorter way to say "stay".

searchDocs.title: Debug views are cheap​
searchDocs.content: StateLabel and PathVisual exist so you never have to print. Make them right after Build() and destroy them with the agent.

searchDocs.title: Noise​
searchDocs.content: Player jumps, the orange pad on the map and the Guardian's alarm all fire one Signalthat the Stalker's Hearing sense listens to. That is the whole integration: the game owns the signal, the sense subscribes, and an agent may fire it too. Fire it from a door slam, a dropped object, a gunshot.  For sounds the world is already playing there is nothing to fire: tag the Sound withCollectionService and give the agent a Sounds sense. It judges every tagged, playing, 3D sound each tick by the volume it would have at the agent (the sound's own Volumeand roll-off), times an AI_SOUND/Multiplier attribute on the sound when you want it to matter more or less, and writes the loudest as HeardSound with its position and distance. A state investigates it the same way the Stalker investigates a noise, reading HeardSoundPosition and HeardSoundAt.  CollectionService:AddTag(radio.Sound, "AI_SOUND") radio.Sound:SetAttribute("AI_SOUND/Multiplier", 2) :AddSense(VluxyAI.Senses.Sounds.new({ Threshold = 0.1 }))

searchDocs.title: The Weeping Angel rule​
searchDocs.content: Dormant until it sees someone. Then it advances only while IsWatched is false, freezes the tick anyone looks, strikes when close, and goes dormant again once Sight's memory of the last position expires. The "looking" check runs from the players' side: the observer's head facing, a cone, and a line of sight to the rig.

searchDocs.title: The two pieces​
searchDocs.content: Broadcaster watches an agent on the server. It fires StateChanged on every state change, EventSent for everything the agent emits, and, at a rate you choose, PositionChanged with the rig's pivot position and a yaw. Snapshot() is for a player who just joined. Make the broadcaster before agent:Start() so the first state is relayed.  Replica lives on the client with a rig and a table of client states, theVisuals. SetState(name) runs the old state's Exit and the new one's Enter;Receive(name, payload) hands an event to your On(name, ...) handlers; SetPosition gives it somewhere to smooth toward. Visuals have the same Enter, Update, Exit shape as a brain, with the replica in place of the agent. That is your custom client logic: a highlight while it hunts, a heartbeat sound while it advances, a camera shake on a scream.  -- server. Id: the rig itself while every client already has it; a string key under streaming. local broadcaster = VluxyAI.Sync.Broadcaster.new(agent, { PositionRate = 0 }) broadcaster.StateChanged:Connect(function(state) syncRemote:FireAllClients({ Kind = "State", Id = model, State = state }) end) broadcaster.EventSent:Connect(function(name, payload) syncRemote:FireAllClients({ Kind = "Event", Id = model, Event = name, Payload = payload }) end) -- client local replica = VluxyAI.Sync.Replica.new({ Entity = model, Visuals = { Hunt = { Enter = function(replica) replica.Data.Glow.Enabled = true end, Exit = function(replica) replica.Data.Glow.Enabled = false end, }, }, }) syncRemote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(message) if message.Kind == "State" then replica:SetState(message.State) elseif message.Kind == "Event" then replica:Receive(message.Event, message.Payload) end end)

searchDocs.title: Ids over the wire​
searchDocs.content: The playground sends the rig itself as the id, which is fine while the rig has replicated to every client (the test place has streaming off and spawns before anyone joins). WithStreamingEnabled, an instance that has not streamed in arrives as nil; send a string key instead (a SyncId attribute, a name) and resolve the rig lazily on the client.

searchDocs.title: Mirror or puppet​
searchDocs.content: Mirror is the simple mode and what the playground uses. The server rig is visible and replicates through Roblox as any NPC does. The replica only runs visuals on it. Send states and events; leave PositionRate at 0.  Puppet is the mode from the design plan: the server keeps a logical position, usually with theCFrame mover on an invisible collider, and each client draws its own rig. Make the replica with Puppet = true, stream positions at ten or so a second over an unreliable remote, and the replica smooths its rig toward each sample so the rate never shows. Kills are still decided on the server from the server position; the client draws the enemy slightly behind, and a hard cut hides the gap.

searchDocs.title: Kills​
searchDocs.content: Kill gives an agent two ways to finish a character, both decided on the server and both announced as a "Kill" event with { Kind, Victim, Duration }:  Live: VluxyAI.Combat.Kill.Live(agent, character, { KillerAnimation, VictimAnimation })takes the victim's root for the server, holds them in a pose next to the killer while both rigs play their animation, and kills them when it ends. Everyone sees it.Black box: VluxyAI.Combat.Kill.BlackBox(agent, character) announces at once and kills after a short delay. The client cuts to black on the event and the death happens behind it.  Both return a handle with Finished and Cancel. A kill that was announced and then cancelled (the attack state was left early, the killer was destroyed, someone else got the victim first) emits "KillCancelled" so the client can take its screen down. On the client:  replica:On("Kill", function(event) if event.Victim ~= Players.LocalPlayer.Character then return end if event.Kind == "BlackBox" then showBlackScreen(event.Duration + 1) else lockCameraOn(replica.Entity, event.Duration) end end)   The playground's Stalker finishes you with a live kill and its Weeping Angel with a black-box one;examples/Client/Kills.luau is the presentation.

searchDocs.title: Anything else​
searchDocs.content: agent:Emit("Scream") from a state, replica:On("Scream", ...) on the client. Emit is the general channel; kills are just its first customer.

searchDocs.title: Wally​
searchDocs.content: Add it to your project's wally.toml under [dependencies]. The package is shared realm, so it can live in a folder both server and client see; only the server needs to build agents, but the types, the runner and the scoring are safe to require anywhere.  [package] name = "your_name/your_project" version = "0.1.0" registry = "https://github.com/UpliftGames/wally-index" realm = "shared" [dependencies] VluxyAI = "greenviper126/vluxyai@0.2.1"   Run wally install. Wally creates a Packages folder holding VluxyAI. It has no dependencies of its own.

searchDocs.title: Rojo​
searchDocs.content: Sync the Packages folder somewhere both realms can reach:  { "name": "your_project", "tree": { "$className": "DataModel", "ReplicatedStorage": { "$className": "ReplicatedStorage", "Packages": { "$path": "Packages" } } } }   Then in a server script:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxyAI = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxyAI)

searchDocs.title: Types across the package boundary​
searchDocs.content: Wally's link files do not carry Luau types by default. If you want VluxyAI.Agent,VluxyAI.Brain and friends to resolve in your editor, runwally-package-types after wally install:  rojo sourcemap default.project.json -o sourcemap.json wally-package-types --sourcemap sourcemap.json Packages/

searchDocs.title: The loop in twenty lines​
searchDocs.content: Patrol, hear something, go and look, spot the player, hunt, lose them, search, give up. Written with When, States and interrupts, the brain is the list of those words:  local States, When = VluxyAI.States, VluxyAI.When local Brain: VluxyAI.Brain = { Initial = "Patrol", Interrupts = { { To = "Hunt", When = When.Has("SeenTarget"), Except = { "Hunt", "Attack" } }, { To = "Investigate", When = When.New("HeardAt"), Except = { "Hunt", "Attack" } }, }, States = { Patrol = States.Patrol({ Points = "Nodes", Speed = 10 }), Investigate = States.Investigate({ Target = "HeardPosition", Then = "Search" }), Hunt = { Enter = function(agent) agent:SetSpeed(15) end, Transitions = { { To = "Attack", When = When.Below("SeenDistance", 4) }, { To = "Search", When = When.Missing("SeenPosition") }, }, Update = function(agent) agent.Data.LastSeen = agent.Blackboard.SeenPosition agent:MoveTo(agent.Blackboard.SeenPosition) return nil end, }, Search = States.Search({ Around = "LastSeen", Radius = 12, Duration = 14, Then = "Patrol" }), Attack = VluxyAI.Combat.Attack.State({ Damage = 34, Cooldown = 1.8, TargetKey = "SeenTarget", Then = "Hunt", Kill = "Live" }), }, }   An interrupt is a transition that applies from every state, checked before the state's own.When.New("HeardAt") is true once per noise: it acknowledges the value as it fires, so the same noise is not investigated every tick. The ready-made states keep their scratch in agent.Dataand skip a point the navigator cannot reach.

searchDocs.title: Seeing in the dark​
searchDocs.content: Sight is binary by default: in the cone with a clear ray is seen. Three options turn it into a horror sense.  Darkness. Visibility is a function of the agent and a target root that scales the sight range for that target. Tag the lights that matter with AI_LIGHT and passPerception.LightAt: a player in the dark is invisible until a light finds them, and a lit flashlight gives them away.Glass. SeeThrough = VluxyAI.Perception.Transparent() lets the ray look past transparent parts. Without it a window blocks sight like a wall.Hiding spots. Set the AI_HIDDEN attribute to true on a character while they are in a locker or under a bed, and Perception.AliveRoots leaves them out. That is the default target list of every sense, so one flag hides a player from Sight, Proximity and Watched together.  :AddSense(VluxyAI.Senses.Sight.new({ Range = 40, Visibility = function(_, root) return VluxyAI.Perception.LightAt(root.Position, 0.1) end, SeeThrough = VluxyAI.Perception.Transparent(), }))

searchDocs.title: Searching like a creature​
searchDocs.content: An enemy never reads a player's position. It knows what its senses wrote and nothing else, so the question is what it does once it has lost you. Three pieces answer it.  Prediction. Sight keeps SeenVelocity and carries PredictedPosition forward for up toPredict seconds after losing you: not where you were, where you were going. Search there first.Points of interest. An Interest map holds the places a player would plausibly be, each with a strength: lockers, doorways, the generator. The game raises a point when something happens near it, and it drifts back. Best scores strength, distance and how long since this enemy looked there, so a group spreads out and nobody checks the same locker twice running.Roaming. States.Roam walks the best point, lingers, marks it visited and asks again, until nothing is worth a look or its time is up.  local interest = VluxyAI.Interest.new() for _, locker in CollectionService:GetTagged("Locker") do interest:Add(locker, { Position = locker.Position, Tags = { "Hiding" } }) end noises:Connect(function(position, loudness) interest:BumpNear(position, 15, loudness or 1) end) Search = States.Search({ Around = "PredictedPosition", Duration = 8, Then = "Roam" }), Roam = States.Roam({ Interest = interest, Duration = 40, Then = "Patrol" }),   That is the shape of a creature that has to look: a guess at where you went, then the likely places in order of likelihood and nearness.

searchDocs.title: A detection meter​
searchDocs.content: A stealth enemy does not hunt the instant a player crosses its cone. Awarenessreads what Sight, Hearing and Sounds wrote and keeps one meter: it rises while a target is in view, jumps on a noise, drains in silence, and passes through Suspicious on the way toAlerted. It also keeps one LastKnownPosition, whichever sense supplied it last, so the brain has a single place to go and look.  :AddSense(VluxyAI.Senses.Sight.new({ Range = 40 })) :AddSense(VluxyAI.Senses.Hearing.new(noises)) :AddSense(VluxyAI.Senses.Awareness.new({ Rise = 0.8, Fall = 0.2 })) Interrupts = { { To = "Hunt", When = When.Equals("AwarenessLevel", "Alerted"), Except = { "Hunt", "Attack" } }, { To = "Investigate", When = When.Equals("AwarenessLevel", "Suspicious"), Except = { "Hunt", "Attack", "Investigate" } }, }, Investigate = States.Investigate({ Target = "LastKnownPosition", Then = "Patrol" }),   Add it after the senses it reads.

searchDocs.title: Sound​
searchDocs.content: Two senses hear. Hearing is for events your code fires on a signal: a jump, a door slam, a gunshot. Sounds is for the Sound instances already playing in the world: tag one with AI_SOUND, keep it on a part so it is 3D, and every agent judges it by the volume it would have at their position, using the sound's own roll-off. An AI_SOUND/Multiplierattribute makes a sound matter more or less to the AI without changing what players hear.  Both take Occlusion, a per-wall multiplier: with Occlusion = 0.5 a noise is half as loud through one wall and a quarter through two. Rays are only cast for noises that would have been heard in the open.

searchDocs.title: Doors​
searchDocs.content: A door is a labelled step, and there are two ways to author one. Both reach the same handler.  Navmesh. Put a PathfindingLink across the doorway (two attachments, one on each side) with Label = "Door", or a PathfindingModifier with PassThrough and the label. Roblox plans through it and marks the crossing waypoint. The step arrives without an Instance, so tag the door part AI_DOOR and give the handler the tag; the nearest tagged instance is looked up for it. No nodes to author.Graph. A link written as { To = 7, Label = "Door", Instance = door }, or in a place aLink ObjectValue with a Label attribute and an Instance child. The navmesh never crosses the door, so a closed door being solid is simply right, and links can be one-way or closed.  :OnStep("Door", function(agent, step) local door = step.Instance if door:GetAttribute("Locked") then return false, 15 -- could not; plan around it for fifteen seconds end Doors.Open(door) task.wait(0.4) return true end, { Tag = "AI_DOOR" })   The navigator stops the mover at the step, reports Interacting, runs the handler, and walks the rest of the path when it returns. A handler that returns false gives the path up asFailed and tells the pathfinder to Close the step: a Graph closes the link, a Navmesh refuses paths through that crossing, and a Ladder orHybrid passes it on. The next plan goes another way, or fails, and the brain does what it does on a failed path. A monster that breaks doors is a handler that plays an animation, unlocks the door and returns true.

searchDocs.title: Scares that do not kill​
searchDocs.content: Kill = "Scare" on the attack state makes every blow a grab: the same hold and animations as a live kill, Damage dealt as the victim is let go, no death, announced as "Scare" so the client can do its jump scare. Kill.Scare is the same thing for a state of your own. A game that keeps health somewhere other than the Humanoid gives the attack state aHealth provider with Get, Damage and optionally Kill.

searchDocs.title: Standing still, staring, vanishing​
searchDocs.content: agent:SetSpeed(speed, seconds) ramps to a speed over time, so a lunge builds and a stop settles instead of snapping.  agent:LookAt(position) turns the body toward a point while it stands. nil stops.agent:Pause() freezes the agent for a cutscene or a jumpscare: no ticks, no movement, timers on hold. Resume picks up where it left off and re-plans to its target.agent:Teleport(position) puts it somewhere else at once. AskPerception.SeenByAnyone first, so a stalker only ever vanishes and reappears off screen.

searchDocs.title: Where the player is really looking​
searchDocs.content: The Watched sense judges "looking" by the head's facing, which on a default rig is the walk direction. For a Weeping Angel or a "do not look at it" monster, replicate the camera with Look: one RemoteEvent, Look.Report on the client, Look.Receive on the server, and its Eye handed to Watched. The server places the camera's rotation at the player's head, so a camera peeking over a wall does not count.

searchDocs.title: More than one monster​
searchDocs.content: Claims is a shared "who is on what" table: an enemy claims a player before chasing, and the others score that player low. Director is the game's hand on the group: a tension meter it raises on kills and near misses that drains by itself, a difficulty number, and a blackboard every enemy in the group can read and write throughdirector:Sense(). A state scales itself with one line:  agent:SetSpeed(director:Scale(BASE_SPEED, 0.5)) -- up to half again at full tension   Every built-in sense has Configure, so the director can widen a cone or shorten a memory mid-round without rebuilding the agent.  Bodies are the other half. Neighbours is one instance shared by a group: every enemy that adds it sees the others as NearbyAgents, NearestAgentDistance, Crowdingand SeparationDirection. Two options turn the knowledge into behaviour, and both are off unless asked for, because a swarm should crowd:  local crowd = VluxyAI.Senses.Neighbours.new({ Range = 10, Slow = { Distance = 5, Min = 0.5 }, -- ease to half speed as the nearest neighbour closes in Avoid = { Radius = 4 }, -- push the mover sideways within four studs }) :AddSense(crowd) -- on each enemy in the group   Slow goes through agent:SetSpeedScale, a multiplier kept on top of whatever speed a state asks for. Avoid goes through the mover's SetNudge, which aims at every step but the last plus the offset. Two groups that should ignore each other use two instances; Filter excludes one kind from another; one enemy opts out of a shared group for itself withagent.Data.Neighbours = { Avoid = false }. A Deadband on Avoid stops the nudge flickering when neighbours keep moving.  Enemies also hear each other. Give a mover Noise = { Signal = noises, Interval = 0.5 } and it fires the same signal the Hearing sense listens to as it walks, so a pack converges on a fight without any wiring in your states.  The player's ears are the client's business: Footsteps on the replica's rig plays a step every few studs of measured movement, locally, with no message from the server.

searchDocs.title: Seeing what it senses​
searchDocs.content: SenseVisual draws the sight cone (green while something is seen), the hearing and proximity circles, and markers at the last seen, predicted and last known positions, so ranges are tuned by eye. Builder:SetStrictBlackboard() makes the agent warn when a state reads a key that looks like a typo of one a sense wrote, which is most of what a typed blackboard would have caught, without the type plumbing.

searchDocs.title: Keeping it cheap​
searchDocs.content: Sight costs a ray per target per tick. Wrap it in Throttle to run it every 0.3 seconds while the brain keeps its 0.1 tick, and give each sense a Prefix when an enemy needs two of the same kind (peripheral and focused vision, say).

searchDocs.title: A sense​
searchDocs.content: Anything with Tick(self, agent, deltaTime), called with a colon once per tick before the brain. The built-ins are Sight, Proximity, Hearing,Sounds (the tagged Sound instances the world is playing, rolled off by distance),Awareness (a detection meter fed by the others), Watched,Surroundings (a ring of rays for the nearest obstacle and the most open direction) and Neighbours (the other agents of a group, with an optional speed ease and sideways nudge), plus Throttle to run any of them less often; the playground's Hunter carries a stamina sense written in a dozen lines. Every built-in takes a Prefix so two of a kind can coexist, and has Configure to change its options after construction. It writes to agent.Blackboard and reads nothing from states. Document the keys you write, usemath.huge for a distance with nothing to measure, and keep memory (a SeenAt-style timestamp) on the blackboard rather than in the sense, so one instance can serve many agents. The agent's position is agent:GetPosition(); Perception has the alive player roots, cone and line-of-sight helpers the built-in senses use.  local Fear = {} Fear.__index = Fear function Fear.new(threshold: number) return setmetatable({ _threshold = threshold }, Fear) end -- Writes: Afraid (boolean) function Fear.Tick(self, agent, deltaTime) local humanoid = agent.Entity:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") -- the agent's own agent.Blackboard.Afraid = humanoid ~= nil and humanoid.Health < self._threshold end return Fear   Destroy(self, agent) is optional. It is called once per agent that is destroyed, with that agent, so a sense that holds something outside itself (a signal connection, asHearing does) releases that agent's share and lets go entirely when none remain.  :AddSense(Fear.new(30))

searchDocs.title: A pathfinder​
searchDocs.content: Anything with FindPath(self, from, to, agent) -> (Path?, reason?). It may yield. from is the mover's root position and to is wherever the state asked to go; return a list of steps whosePosition is a floor position, or nil and a short reason.  A pathfinder that can tell when the world changes under its last path may also carry a Blockedsignal (VluxyAI.Signal.new()). Fire it with no arguments and the navigator re-plans on its next cadence tick instead of waiting for the mover's stuck check. Navmesh relays thePath.Blocked event this way; a pathfinder that cannot know simply leaves the field out.  local Teleporters = {} Teleporters.__index = Teleporters function Teleporters.new(pads) return setmetatable({ Name = "Teleporters", _pads = pads }, Teleporters) end function Teleporters.FindPath(self, from, to, agent) local pad = self:_nearestPad(from) if pad == nil then return nil, "no pad near" end return { { Position = pad.Entrance, Action = "Custom", Label = "Teleport" }, { Position = to, Action = "Walk" }, } end return Teleporters   Compose it with the built-ins through a Ladder, which tries each in order. Give every rung the same AgentRadius and AgentHeight; each measures the body on its own.  :UsePathfinder(VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Ladder.new({ VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Straight.new(), Teleporters.new(pads), VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Navmesh.new(), }))   For a level with doors, one-way drops or rooms the navmesh cannot connect, the package already has the two pieces the design plan calls for: a Graph of hand-placed nodes with A*, read out of a folder of parts with Graph.FromInstances, and a Hybrid that uses your local pathfinder up close and the graph for long legs, refining both ends locally.  -- once, for the level: reading the folder casts a ray per pair of nodes local graph = VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Graph.FromInstances(workspace.NavGraph) -- per agent: the local pathfinder holds a navmesh Path of its own :UsePathfinder(VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Hybrid.new({ Graph = graph, Local = VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Ladder.new({ VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Straight.new(), VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Navmesh.new(), }), LocalRadius = 40, }))   A door is a Custom step on a graph link: the game listens to agent.Navigator.StepReached, stops the agent, opens the door, and calls MoveTo again.

searchDocs.title: A mover​
searchDocs.content: Anything with Follow(path), Stop(), GetPosition(), GetSpeed(), SetSpeed(speed),IsMoving(), and two signals: StepReached and Arrived. The rules that keep it honest with the Navigator, all listed on Types.Mover:  Follow fires Arrived(false) for the path it replaces, before starting the new one, and must not yield: the navigator calls it from its planning thread.The new path's outcome is reported on a later frame, never from inside Follow:Arrived(true) once the last step is reached (fire StepReached for it first), Arrived(false)when stuck. An empty path is Arrived(false) on the next frame.Stop fires Arrived(false) if a path was in progress, and nothing otherwise.Steps are floor positions; add your own height. GetPosition returns the body, not the floor.  What the navigator does with the outcome: on true it checks the target against ArriveDistanceand either reports arrival or re-plans; on false it re-plans on its cadence.  Make the signals with VluxyAI.Signal.new(). Read CFrameMover for a small complete one; it is what a server-side "logical position" agent with no rig uses.

searchDocs.title: Doors and other scripted steps​
searchDocs.content: A pathfinder may emit a step with a Label (and usually Action = "Custom"): a PathfindingModifierlabel from the navmesh, or a Graph link written as { To = 7, Label = "Door", Instance = door }. Register what to do there with Builder:OnStep:  :OnStep("Door", function(agent, step) Doors.Open(step.Instance) task.wait(0.4) end)   When the mover reaches the step the navigator stops it, reports Interacting throughagent:GetPathStatus(), runs the handler in its own thread, and walks the rest of the path when it returns. A state that calls MoveTo every tick with the same target keeps waiting; a new target or Stop abandons the path. Nothing in the package knows what a door is; it only knows where to pause. agent.Navigator.StepReached still fires for every step, handled or not.  A handler returning false (and optionally a number of seconds) means the step could not be taken: the path is Failed and the pathfinder's optional Close(step, seconds) is called so the next plan avoids it. A navmesh step has no Instance; pass { Tag = "AI_DOOR" } as the third argument of OnStep and the nearest tagged instance is filled in first.  In a place, a Link ObjectValue under a graph node takes Action and Label attributes and anInstance ObjectValue child pointing at the door, and Graph.FromInstances reads them.

searchDocs.title: Content modules​
searchDocs.content: A brain can be its own module. Cast it on the way out so a missing field fails in the editor:  return Stalker :: VluxyAI.Brain   VluxyAI.ValidateBrain(Stalker, "Stalker") runs the same checks at runtime, with Stalker. as the prefix of any error, for a test that walks a folder of enemies.

searchDocs.title: Why it is shaped like this​
searchDocs.content: States never query the world. Senses write what they notice to agent.Blackboard; states read it. That is what keeps a brain table readable, and what lets the whole thing run under Lune with fakes.Modes are transitions, targets are scores. A state's transitions are checked in order every tick and the first true one wins, so mode changes are deterministic. When a state has to choosewhich player or which room, Utility scoring picks one; a bad score gives an odd choice, never an oscillating AI.Contracts, not registries. You never register a pathfinder kind or an enemy kind by name. You pass your own module in, and Build() checks its shape. A mistake reads asDefinition.Brain.States.Hunt.Transitions[2].To = "Chase" names no state.  Read Installation to add the package, then Your first AI to build one.

searchDocs.title: Connection​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Connection { Connected: boolean-- false once disconnected. Disconnect: (self: Connection) → ()-- Disconnects the handler. } What Types.Signal Connect returns. Any cleanup helper that calls Disconnect accepts it.

searchDocs.title: Signal<T...>​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Signal<T...> { Connect: ( self: Signal<T...>, handler: (T...) → () ) → Connection-- Runs handler on every fire. Once: ( self: Signal<T...>, handler: (T...) → () ) → Connection-- Runs handler on the next fire only. Wait: (self: Signal<T...>) → T...-- Yields until the next fire. Fire: ( self: Signal<T...>, T... ) → ()-- Fires every connected handler. DisconnectAll: (self: Signal<T...>) → ()-- Drops every handler. Destroy: (self: Signal<T...>) → ()-- Drops every handler and refuses new ones. } A small signal with the same surface as RBXScriptSignal, implemented in plain Luau so the core runs outside Roblox. Movers and agents expose these; a Cleaner releases their connections.

searchDocs.title: StepAction​
searchDocs.content: </> type StepAction = "Walk" | "Jump" | "Custom" What a Types.Mover does at a step. Mirrors Enum.PathWaypointAction. Custom steps come from PathfindingModifier labels or your own pathfinder; the mover walks to them like any other step and the Types.Navigator's StepReached tells you when it got there, so a door or a ladder is your code.

searchDocs.title: Step​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Step { Position: Vector3 -- Where to go, as a floor position. Movers add their own height. Action: StepAction-- What to do on the way there. Label: string?-- The PathfindingModifier label, or whatever your pathfinder attaches. A Types.StepHandler registered for it runs when the step is reached. Instance: Instance? -- What the step is about, when the pathfinder knows: the door on a Graph link. } One point along a Types.Path.

searchDocs.title: StepHandler​
searchDocs.content: </> type StepHandler = ( agent: Agent, step: Step, index: number ) → ( boolean?, number? ) What happens at a labelled step: open the door, climb the ladder, play the vault. Registered with Builder:OnStep under the step's Label. Runs in its own thread and may yield; the navigator holds the mover at the step, reports Interacting, and walks the rest of the path when the handler returns. A new target or Stop while it runs abandons the path; the handler should check Agent:IsDestroyed after a long yield. Return false to say the step could not be taken (a locked door). The path is given up as Failed, and the pathfinder is told to Close that step for the seconds given as the second return (default 10), so the next plan goes another way. Returning nothing or true means the step was taken.

searchDocs.title: StepRegistration​
searchDocs.content: </> interface StepRegistration { Handler: StepHandler Tag: string?-- When the step arrives without an Instance (a navmesh link or modifier), the nearest instance carrying this CollectionService tag within Radius of the step is put in step.Instance before the handler runs. Radius: number?-- Studs. Default 8. } What Builder:OnStep stores for a label: the handler, and how to find the door for a step that does not already know it. A plain Types.StepHandler is accepted wherever this is.

searchDocs.title: Path​
searchDocs.content: </> type Path = {Step} An ordered list of steps from where the agent was to where it wants to be. The first step is the agent's own position when the pathfinder includes it; movers cope either way.

searchDocs.title: Pathfinder​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Pathfinder { FindPath: ( self: any, from: Vector3 , to: Vector3 , agent: Agent ) → ( Path?, string? )-- Returns a path, or nil and a reason. May yield. Destroy: ((self: any) → ())?-- Optional cleanup. Called when the agent is destroyed. Name: string?-- Used in messages, such as a Ladder's joined reasons. Blocked: Signal<()>?-- Optional. Fired when the world changes under the last path returned; the Navigator re-plans on its cadence. Close: (( self: any, step: Step, seconds: number ) → ())?-- Optional. A labelled step could not be taken (a locked door): plan around it for seconds. Graph closes the link, Navmesh refuses paths through it; Ladder and Hybrid pass it on. } Plans and nothing else. A pathfinder never moves the agent, never creates parts and never keeps a target. from and to may be at any height: from is the mover's root and to is often a player's root or a floor node; the path it returns holds floor positions. An empty path counts as a failure. FindPath runs in its own thread and may yield or error; an error is treated as a failed plan and warned about once. VluxyAI.Pathfinders ships Navmesh, Straight and Ladder; your own is any table with FindPath. Blocked is how a pathfinder that watches the world (Navmesh listens to its Path.Blocked) tells the navigator that the path being walked is no longer good, so the agent re-plans as soon as the cadence allows instead of walking into the obstacle and waiting for the mover's stuck check. A pathfinder that cannot know leaves it out; Ladder and Hybrid forward it from the rung that produced the current path.

searchDocs.title: Mover​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Mover { Follow: ( self: any, path: Path ) → ()-- Starts moving along path, replacing any current path. Stop: (self: any) → ()-- Halts. Fires Arrived(false) if a path was in progress. GetPosition: (self: any) → Vector3 -- Where the agent's root or pivot is right now: the body, not the floor. GetSpeed: (self: any) → number-- Studs per second. SetSpeed: ( self: any, speed: number ) → ()-- Studs per second. IsMoving: (self: any) → boolean-- true while a path is in progress. StepReached: Signal<( number, Step )>-- Fired with the index and step each time one is reached. Arrived: Signal<boolean>-- Fired once per Follow: true at the end of the path, false if stopped, replaced or stuck. Destroy: ((self: any) → ())?-- Optional cleanup. Called when the agent is destroyed. Face: (( self: any, position: Vector3? ) → ())?-- Optional. Turn toward position while standing still; nil stops. Agent:LookAt calls it. Teleport: (( self: any, position: Vector3 ) → ())?-- Optional. Put the body at position at once, dropping any path. Agent:Teleport calls it. SetNudge: (( self: any, offset: Vector3? ) → ())?-- Optional. Aim at each step plus offset (never the last step), so a steering sense can push the body sideways; nil clears. Neighbours calls it. } Executes a Types.Path and nothing else. Rules that keep a mover and the Navigator honest: Follow fires Arrived(false) for the path it replaces before starting the new one, and the new path's outcome is reported on a later frame, never from inside Follow. An empty path is Arrived(false) on the next frame. Follow is called from the navigator's planning thread, so it must not yield. Arrived(true) means the last step was reached. The navigator then checks the target for itself: within ArriveDistance it reports arrival, otherwise it re-plans or reports failure. Arrived(false) from a stuck detector makes the navigator re-plan on its cadence. VluxyAI.Movers ships Humanoid (uses MoveTo) and CFrame (steps a pivot, no rig needed); your own is any table with this shape. Make the signals with VluxyAI.Signal.new().

searchDocs.title: Blackboard​
searchDocs.content: </> type Blackboard = {[string]: any} The only thing states read about the world. Senses write to it every tick; states and utility considerations read it and never query the world themselves. Each sense documents the keys it writes. Declare your own blackboard type per AI and cast once at the boundary.

searchDocs.title: Sense​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Sense { Tick: ( self: any, agent: Agent, deltaTime: number ) → ()-- Called once per agent tick. Writes to agent.Blackboard. Destroy: (( self: any, agent: Agent? ) → ())?-- Optional cleanup, called with each agent that is destroyed. A shared sense releases that agent's state and tears down only when none remain; called with no agent it tears down outright. Configure: (( self: any, patch: {[string]: any} ) → ())?-- Optional. Changes options after construction; every built-in has it, so a director can widen a cone or shorten a memory mid-round. } Perceives and nothing else. Senses tick in the order they were added, before the navigator and the brain. A sense keeps no per-agent state of its own: memory (SeenAt, HeardAt) lives on the blackboard, so one instance may serve many agents and a state may clear a memory early by setting the key to nil. Distances are math.huge when there is nothing to measure. VluxyAI.Senses ships Sight, Proximity, Hearing, Sounds, Awareness, Watched, Surroundings and Neighbours; your own is any table with Tick.

searchDocs.title: Transition​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Transition { To: string-- The state to enter. Must exist in the brain; Build() checks. When: (agent: Agent) → boolean-- Checked every tick, in order, before Update. } A declarative transition. The first one whose When returns true wins. To may name the current state, which re-enters it (Exit then Enter); an Update returning the current name does nothing. If When forces a change through Agent:SetState, that change wins and its own result is ignored.

searchDocs.title: Interrupt​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Interrupt { To: string-- The state to enter. Must exist in the brain; Build() checks. When: (agent: Agent) → boolean-- Checked every tick, in order, before the current state's own transitions. Except: {string}?-- States in which this interrupt is not checked, such as the one it leads to or an attack that must finish. } A Types.Transition that applies from every state: "hunt whoever I see", "freeze when lit", "stop when the director says so". Written once on the brain instead of in every state. Interrupts are checked in order before the current state's transitions; the first true one wins the tick.

searchDocs.title: State​
searchDocs.content: </> interface State { Enter: ((agent: Agent) → ())?-- Runs once when the state becomes current. Update: (( agent: Agent, deltaTime: number ) → string?)?-- Runs every tick. Return a state name to change state, or nothing to stay. Exit: ((agent: Agent) → ())?-- Runs once when the state stops being current. Transitions: {Transition}?-- Checked in order before Update each tick. } One state of a Types.Brain. Every field is optional, so a state can be as small as a single Update. Returning the current state's name from Update does nothing; use Agent:SetState to re-enter a state on purpose. If Update itself forces a change through SetState, its return value is ignored so two transitions never stack.

searchDocs.title: Brain​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Brain { Initial: string-- The state entered on Start(). States: {[string]: State}-- Every state, keyed by name. Interrupts: {Interrupt}?-- Transitions that apply from every state, checked before the current state's own. } A flat finite state machine as a table. The whole AI, readable top to bottom.

searchDocs.title: Curve​
searchDocs.content: </> type Curve = (x: number) → number Maps a normalised input in [0, 1] to a score in [0, 1]. Utility.Curves ships the common shapes; any function works.

searchDocs.title: Consideration<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Consideration<T> { Input: ( agent: Agent, candidate: T ) → number-- Reads a raw value about the candidate, usually off the blackboard. Min: number?-- The raw value that maps to 0. Default 0. Max: number?-- The raw value that maps to 1. Default 1. Curve: Curve?-- The response curve. Default linear. Invert: boolean?-- Flip the normalised input before the curve, so a big distance scores low. } One factor in scoring a candidate. A candidate's score is the product of its considerations, so any one of them can veto by returning 0.

searchDocs.title: Scored<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Scored<T> { Candidate: T-- The thing that was scored. Score: number-- Its score in [0, 1]. } One row of a Utility.ScoreAll result.

searchDocs.title: PathStatus​
searchDocs.content: </> type PathStatus = "Idle" | "Planning" | "Moving" | "Interacting" | "Arrived" | "Failed" Where a Navigator is with its current target. Idle means no target or stopped; Interacting means a Types.StepHandler is running at a step and the walk resumes after.

searchDocs.title: NavigationOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface NavigationOptions { RepathInterval: number?-- Seconds between re-plans while the target keeps moving. Must be above 0; the three distances below may be 0. Default 0.5. RepathDistance: number?-- Studs the target must move before a re-plan happens. Default 2. MaxPathAge: number?-- Seconds a path is followed before it is planned again even though the target has not moved, so the agent keeps up with a changing level. Must be above 0. Default math.huge (never). ArriveDistance: number?-- Horizontal studs from the target that count as arrived. Must exceed the two bodies' radii for a chase to ever arrive. Default 2.5. ArriveHeight: number?-- Height difference allowed for arrival, so a target on the floor above does not count. Default 8. } Tunes how Navigator turns repeated MoveTo calls into plans.

searchDocs.title: Navigator​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Navigator { MoveTo: ( self: any, target: Vector3 ) → ()-- Head to target. Safe to call every tick; re-plans on a cadence. Stop: (self: any) → ()-- Forget the target and halt. GetStatus: (self: any) → PathStatus-- Where the navigator is with its target. GetTarget: (self: any) → Vector3? -- The current target. GetPath: (self: any) → Path?-- The last path planned. StepReached: Signal<( number, Step )>-- Forwarded from the mover. Arrived: Signal<boolean>-- Fired when the target is reached (true) or given up on (false). PathChanged: Signal<Path?>-- Fired with each new path, and with nil when there is none. } Owns the pair of a Types.Pathfinder and a [Types.Mover]: plans with one, follows with the other, and re-plans when the target moves, the pathfinder reports the path blocked, or the path is older than MaxPathAge. Every agent with both has one at agent.Navigator.

searchDocs.title: AgentDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> interface AgentDefinition { Entity: Model -- The model the AI drives. Needs a PrimaryPart. Brain: Brain-- The state table. Pathfinder: Pathfinder?-- Required if Mover is given. Mover: Mover?-- Required if Pathfinder is given. Senses: {Sense}?-- Ticked in order before the brain each tick. Blackboard: Blackboard?-- Initial blackboard values. Copied per agent. Data: {[string]: any}?-- Initial agent.Data. Copied per agent. Yours to use. Tick: number?-- Seconds between ticks. Default 0.1. Navigation: NavigationOptions?-- Navigator tuning. Steps: {[string]: StepHandler | StepRegistration}?-- What to do at labelled steps, by label. See Builder:OnStep. StrictBlackboard: boolean?-- Warn once when a state reads a blackboard key that looks like a typo of one a sense wrote (SeenTaget). For development; costs a metatable on every read. Default false. Name: string?-- Used in messages. Default Entity.Name. } Everything an Agent is built from. The Builder produces one of these; you can also write it as a table and hand it to VluxyAI.NewAgent. Validate checks it either way.

searchDocs.title: Agent​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Agent { Entity: Model -- The model being driven. Name: string-- For messages. Blackboard: Blackboard-- Written by senses, read by states. Data: {[string]: any}-- Free scratch space for your states. Brain: Brain-- The state table. Senses: {Sense}-- Ticked before the brain. Navigator: Navigator?-- Present when the definition had a pathfinder and a mover. Mover: Mover?-- The mover, if any. Pathfinder: Pathfinder?-- The pathfinder, if any. StateChanged: Signal<( string, string? )>-- Fired with the new and previous state names. Destroyed: Signal<()>-- Fired once, at the end of Destroy, so anything built around the agent can go with it. Events: Signal<( string, any )>-- Everything the agent announces through Agent:Emit; a Broadcaster relays it to clients. GetState: (self: Agent) → string?-- The current state name, nil before Start. SetState: ( self: Agent, name: string ) → ()-- Force a transition, re-entering if already there. MoveTo: ( self: Agent, target: Vector3 ) → ()-- Shorthand for Navigator:MoveTo. Errors without a navigator; warns and does nothing before Start. Stop: (self: Agent) → ()-- Shorthand for Navigator:Stop. No-op without a navigator. GetPosition: (self: Agent) → Vector3 -- The mover's position, or the entity's pivot. HasArrived: (self: Agent) → boolean-- true while the navigator status is Arrived. GetPathStatus: (self: Agent) → PathStatus-- The navigator status, or Idle without a navigator. SetSpeed: ( self: Agent, speed: number, seconds: number? ) → ()-- The base speed; the mover gets it times the speed scale. With seconds, ramps there over the ticks. No-op without a mover. SetSpeedScale: ( self: Agent, scale: number ) → ()-- A multiplier layered on the base speed, kept across states. 1 is none. GetSpeedScale: (self: Agent) → number GetSpeed: (self: Agent) → number-- The base speed, before the scale. StartTimer: ( self: Agent, name: string, seconds: number ) → ()-- Starts a named timer. TimerDone: ( self: Agent, name: string ) → boolean-- true once the timer ran out, or if it was never started. TimerLeft: ( self: Agent, name: string ) → number-- Seconds left on the timer, 0 when done. TimeInState: (self: Agent) → number-- Seconds since the current state was entered, paused time excluded. 0 before Start. Pause: (self: Agent) → ()-- Freeze: no ticks, no movement, timers on hold. For cutscenes, jumpscares and a director backing an enemy off. Resume: (self: Agent) → ()-- Undo Pause. The navigator re-plans to its target on the next tick. IsPaused: (self: Agent) → boolean LookAt: ( self: Agent, position: Vector3? ) → ()-- Turn toward position while standing still, nil to stop. Needs a mover with Face; otherwise does nothing. Teleport: ( self: Agent, position: Vector3 ) → ()-- Put the body at position at once, dropping the current path. Uses the mover's Teleport, else the entity's PivotTo. IsNew: ( self: Agent, key: string ) → boolean-- true while Blackboard[key] is non-nil and differs from the value last passed to Acknowledge. Acknowledge: ( self: Agent, key: string ) → ()-- Marks the current Blackboard[key] as dealt with, so IsNew is false until it changes. Step: ( self: Agent, deltaTime: number ) → ()-- One tick, driven by hand. Tests use this. Start: ( self: Agent, manual: boolean? ) → Agent-- Enters the initial state and starts ticking on Heartbeat. With manual, you drive Step yourself. IsRunning: (self: Agent) → boolean-- true between Start and Destroy. IsDestroyed: (self: Agent) → boolean-- true once Destroy has run. Emit: ( self: Agent, name: string, payload: any? ) → ()-- Announces something for clients: a scream, a kill, a door. Fires Events. Destroy: (self: Agent) → ()-- Exits the current state, stops, destroys every part. } The running AI. Handed to every Enter, Update, Exit, When and Input function.

searchDocs.title: ClientState​
searchDocs.content: </> interface ClientState { Enter: ((replica: any) → ())?-- Runs when the server enters the state of that name. Update: (( replica: any, deltaTime: number ) → ())?-- Runs every frame while it is current. Exit: ((replica: any) → ())?-- Runs when the server leaves it. } The client's side of one server state: what a Replica does while the enemy is in it. The same shape as a Types.State without transitions, since the server decides those.

searchDocs.title: Visuals​
searchDocs.content: </> type Visuals = {[string]: ClientState} Client states keyed by server state name. Only the states a client needs to react to are listed; the rest are tracked without doing anything.

searchDocs.title: Snapshot​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Snapshot { State: string?-- The current state name. Position: Vector3 -- The rig's pivot position. Yaw: number-- Facing in radians about Y. } Everything a client that just joined needs, from Broadcaster.Snapshot to Replica.ApplySnapshot.

searchDocs.title: KillKind​
searchDocs.content: </> type KillKind = "Live" | "BlackBox" | "Scare" How a Kill is presented: played out in the world, cut to black, or a scare, which is the live hold without the death.

searchDocs.title: HealthProvider​
searchDocs.content: </> interface HealthProvider { Get: (character: Model ) → number-- The character's current health. Damage: ( character: Model , amount: number ) → ()-- Hurt it. Kill: ((character: Model ) → ())?-- Finish it. Default: Damage with math.huge. } How Attack and Kill read and change a victim's health when the game does not use the Humanoid for it. Without one, the Humanoid's Health and TakeDamage are used.

searchDocs.title: KillEvent​
searchDocs.content: </> interface KillEvent { Kind: KillKind Victim: Model -- The character being killed. Duration: number-- Seconds until the victim dies (or, for a scare, is released), for the client to match. } The payload of the "Kill" event an agent emits, and of the "Scare" event a scare emits. A "KillCancelled" (or "ScareCancelled") event with { Kind, Victim } follows if it ends early.

searchDocs.title: 1. Write the brain​
searchDocs.content: A brain is a table: an Initial state name and a States table. Each state can have Enter,Update, Exit and Transitions, all optional.  local Stalker = { Initial = "Idle", States = { Idle = { Enter = function(agent) agent:Stop() end, Transitions = { { To = "Chase", When = function(agent) return agent.Blackboard.SeenTarget ~= nil end }, }, }, Chase = { Transitions = { { To = "Idle", When = function(agent) return agent.Blackboard.SeenPosition == nil end }, }, Update = function(agent) agent:MoveTo(agent.Blackboard.SeenPosition) end, }, }, }   Every tick the runner checks the current state's transitions in order and takes the first whoseWhen is true. If none fires, Update runs; it may return the name of the next state, or nilto stay. (Under --!strict with the brain annotated as VluxyAI.Brain, write return nilexplicitly: the checker wants every path of Update to return a string?.)  SeenTarget and SeenPosition are written by the Sight sense; the brain never raycasts.

searchDocs.title: 2. Stack the parts​
searchDocs.content: local VluxyAI = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxyAI) local agent = VluxyAI.new(rig) :UseBrain(Stalker) :UsePathfinder(VluxyAI.Pathfinders.Navmesh.new({ AgentRadius = 2, AgentHeight = 5 })) :UseMover(VluxyAI.Movers.Humanoid.new(rig, { Speed = 14 })) :AddSense(VluxyAI.Senses.Sight.new({ Range = 40, FieldOfView = 120, Memory = 3 })) :Build() :Start()   Build() validates everything and errors with the path of the first bad field. Start() enters the initial state and begins ticking on Heartbeat, every 0.1 seconds by default (Builder:SetTick changes it).  The same stack, with the pathfinder, the humanoid mover, Sight and Proximity already chosen:  local agent = VluxyAI.Presets.Humanoid(rig):UseBrain(Stalker):Build():Start()

searchDocs.title: 3. Move​
searchDocs.content: agent:MoveTo(position) is safe to call every tick with a moving target. The Navigatorbehind it plans once, re-plans when the target moves more than a couple of studs, retries when the mover gets stuck, and never plans more often than its RepathInterval. Ask it how things are going with agent:GetPathStatus() (Idle, Planning, Moving, Arrived, Failed) oragent:HasArrived().  A path to a target that stays put is walked to its end. When the level changes under the agent, the Navmesh pathfinder's Blocked signal makes the navigator re-plan on its next cadence tick, and MaxPathAge in Builder:SetNavigation plans again every so many seconds regardless, for the games where a fresh path is worth one ComputeAsync:  :SetNavigation({ MaxPathAge = 2 })   The brain above is written by hand. When and States shorten the common parts, and Interrupts on the brain hold the transitions that apply from every state;Building a horror enemy shows the whole loop in twenty lines.

searchDocs.title: 4. Take it apart​
searchDocs.content: agent:Destroy()   Exits the current state, stops the mover, and destroys the navigator, every sense, the mover and the pathfinder. The rig is yours; the agent never destroys it.

searchDocs.title: Where to put things​
searchDocs.content: agent.Blackboard is what the AI knows. Senses write it; states read it.agent.Data is yours: the current patrol index, the chosen target. Set initial values withBuilder:SetData.Waiting is a timer: agent:StartTimer("Attack", 1) in Enter, agent:TimerDone("Attack") in a transition.Acting on a target goes through Perception:VluxyAI.Perception.HumanoidOf(agent.Blackboard.SeenTarget).Anything that needs the world (a raycast, a distance to a player) belongs in a sense, not a state. If none of the built-in senses fits, write one.
